obj/find-the-note.text: The steward's note, in a cramped hand: 'For the watch, when I am not here: the watch fires on the walls are lit as the household rises. The cook is up first: hers is at the wall walk's end under the kitchen tower. The porter rises next to open the gate: his is at the wall walk's end under the gatehouse. Then the steward: mine is in the turret on the far wall, on the kitchen side. The lord rises last of all: his is in the turret on the far wall, on the gatehouse side. Light one out of turn, and every fire on the walls goes out. B.'

obj/feed-the-cat-1.text: The cat eats the first cod in three bites, eyes closed, like someone who has had cod in a great many harbours and is comparing.

obj/feed-the-cat-2.text: The cat looks at the second cod for a long moment, the way a fencer looks at a stranger's stance, and then eats it anyway.

obj/feed-the-cat-3.text: The cat eats the third cod slowly. 'Cold water. A shady pond. Acceptable.'

obj/feed-the-cat-4.text: The fourth cod goes the way of the others. The cat licks one paw, and for a moment her claws come out, long and very clean.

obj/feed-the-cat-5.text: The cat finishes the fifth cod and sits up, enormous and satisfied. 'Good. Now the cat will show you a friend. A clever friend. Follow. Do not dawdle.'

Halfway down the cliff path a puffin stares at you from a ledge. It leaves a feather behind when it goes, possibly on purpose.
Somebody's grandmother leans out of the terrace cottage's window and presses a twist of paper on you: three biscuits, still warm, for the festival.
